title: Plant Manager-Northeast Water Treatment Plant
text:
**Job Summary**
---------------

Provides leadership and management for treatment plant operations, process control, regulatory compliance, laboratory activities, preventive and corrective maintenance coordination, safety programs, emergency preparedness, employee development, budget administration, inventory control, contractor activities, and facility improvement projects. Evaluates plant performance and treatment processes, establishes operational priorities, develops and implements procedures, and directs corrective actions necessary to maintain treatment quality, regulatory compliance, equipment reliability, and continuity of operations.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

• Recognizes and fulfills the professional and ethical obligations associated with an FDEP treatment operator license. Ensures licensed duties and treatment operations are performed in accordance with FDEP requirements, applicable federal, state, and local laws and standards, permit conditions, County policies, established operating procedures, and safety requirements. Exercises professional judgment in a manner that protects public health, employee safety, water quality, environmental quality, and the integrity of the County's treatment operations.
 
• Plans, directs, manages, and evaluates the operations and activities of an assigned water or wastewater treatment facility to ensure safe, reliable, efficient, and regulatory-compliant operations. Establishes facility priorities, coordinates personnel and resources, evaluates operational performance, and provides overall management and technical direction for treatment processes, maintenance activities, laboratory functions, safety programs, regulatory compliance, and facility support activities.
 
• Supervises, directs, develops, and evaluates assigned employees; coordinates daily work activities; organizes, prioritizes, and assigns work; monitors work in progress and completed work; addresses employee concerns and performance matters; provides coaching, counseling, training, and technical expertise; completes employee performance evaluations; and administers personnel responsibilities consistent with County policies and delegated authority.
 
• Directs and evaluates water treatment processes and equipment applicable to the assigned facility, including pumping, chemical treatment and disinfection, filtration, membrane and reverse osmosis systems, biological treatment, aeration, clarification, sludge and solids handling, storage, wells, and related treatment equipment. Ensures treatment processes are operated and adjusted as necessary to maintain treatment performance, water quality, regulatory compliance, equipment reliability, and continuity of operations.
 
• Evaluates plant performance through SCADA systems, computerized controls, laboratory and process-control results, instrumentation, gauges, meters, alarms, flow conditions, chemical feed rates, equipment performance, treatment loading, and operational trends. Directs appropriate operational adjustments and corrective actions and provides technical direction for complex treatment-process, equipment, mechanical, instrumentation, chemical-feed, and operational problems.
 
• Evaluates laboratory and process-control activities associated with the assigned facility. Ensures required water samples are collected and analyzed in accordance with applicable requirements; reviews laboratory and quality-control results; evaluates treatment trends and compliance data; and directs operational adjustments or additional investigation when results indicate abnormal treatment conditions or potential compliance concerns.
 
• Maintains responsibility for the professional and ethical performance of licensed treatment plant operations within the assigned facility. Ensures operational and regulatory records are accurate, complete, and truthful; reinforces the professional and ethical obligations associated with FDEP licensure; and ensures actual or potential regulatory violations, treatment failures, permit exceedances, unsafe conditions, or environmental concerns are appropriately evaluated, documented, reported, and addressed.
 
• Directs facility safety activities and ensures adherence to established safety procedures and requirements. Monitors workplace conditions and use of required personal protective equipment; ensures appropriate Job Safety Analyses and hazard assessments are completed; supports safety training, inspections, incident investigations, and corrective actions; and takes appropriate action to address unsafe conditions or practices.
 
• Directs and coordinates preventive and corrective maintenance activities involving treatment equipment, instrumentation, buildings, grounds, and other facility assets. Establishes operational and maintenance priorities; coordinates work orders, equipment shutdowns and start-ups, equipment isolation, contractor activities, and return-to-service requirements; and ensures maintenance activities are coordinated to minimize disruption to treatment operations.
 
• Consults with Division management and other appropriate officials regarding development and administration of the facility’s operating budget in accordance with County procedures. Evaluates operational needs, develops budget recommendations, monitors expenditures within approved limits, and supports operating and capital budget development.
 
• Develops and implements short- and long-term operational plans, goals, and objectives for the assigned treatment facility; evaluates plant performance, operational efficiency, treatment processes, procedures, staffing, and resource utilization; identifies opportunities to improve safety, reliability, regulatory compliance, treatment performance, and operational efficiency; and implements appropriate improvements.
 
• Develops, evaluates, updates, and implements standard operating procedures, treatment-process protocols, safety requirements, security procedures, emergency-response plans, disaster-preparedness plans, and other facility programs necessary to support effective and compliant plant operations.
 
• Performs and oversees administrative activities associated with facility operations. Prepares, reviews, approves, or authorizes operational reports, records, purchases, work orders, payroll information, schedules, overtime, specifications, solicitations, procurement documentation, and other administrative materials within delegated authority.
 
• Coordinates capital improvements, construction projects, facility modifications, and contracted services affecting the assigned treatment facility. Provides operational and technical input during planning and design; reviews proposals and project documents; participates in project and bid meetings as appropriate; coordinates construction activities with engineering personnel and contractors; and ensures continuity of treatment operations during construction, expansion, commissioning, and start-up activities.
 
• Directs and monitors facility inventory and asset-management activities. Ensures adequate availability of chemicals, equipment, parts, tools, safety materials, laboratory supplies, and other operational resources; reviews anticipated needs; authorizes or initiates purchases and requisitions within delegated authority; assists with specifications and procurement activities; and ensures appropriate inventory and asset records are maintained.
 
• Responds to complaints, questions, and concerns regarding facility operations or related matters; researches operational issues, coordinates appropriate follow-up, and initiates or directs problem resolution within assigned authority. Performs public-information and community-outreach functions related to the assigned treatment facility. Provides information regarding treatment operations.
 
• Serves as the primary management-level operational contact for the assigned facility and maintains availability consistent with the requirements of a continuous-operation treatment facility. Responds to all significant conditions requiring management-level direction or decision-making.
 
• Follows and ensures compliance with established safety and emergency-response requirements. Recognizes when a conditions exceeds the Plant Manager's delegated authority or technical scope and promptly coordinates with or seeks assistance from Division or Department management, engineering, maintenance, regulatory agencies, emergency-management personnel, legal or risk-management personnel, or other appropriate specialized resources.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

-Vocational/technical degree required.
 
-Seven (7) years of related experience.
 
-Candidates without a degree should possess one (1) additional year of related experience.
 
-Fingerprinting/background screening required.
 
 
LICENSES/CERTIFICATES
 
-Must possess and maintain the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Drinking Water Treatment Operator License required for the assigned facility and position, as applicable.
 
-Driver’s License with any applicable endorsement(s) to drive a county vehicle as provided in CMA 5805.
 
-Maintains all required professional licenses and certifications in good standing and complies with applicable continuing-education and renewal requirements.

**Supplemental information**
----------------------------

Salary offers above the minimum pay grade may be considered based on qualifications.
 
Essential Employees may be required to work during an undeclared or declared emergency. The County’s Administrative Office will determine who will be required to work on an incident-by-incident basis.
 
This job posting is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of responsibilities, skills, or working conditions associated with the position.

***Collier County is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any status protected by applicable law. In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities. Veterans’ Preference is provided to eligible applicants in accordance with Florida law.***
